part1_frame_reproducible.result: both runs produced self_pixel samples of R0 G0 B255 at three positions
part1_frame_reproducible.calls: CreatePrimarySurface, BeginFrame=1, Clear, PresentSurface all returned normally
part1_frame_reproducible.note: an attempt to add SetTargetSurface and SetRenderTarget before BeginFrame turned the frame black, so those calls were reverted; the shipped BeginFrame already establishes the target

part3_what_terrain_and_a_character_requi.geometry_submission: needs a vertex declaration, a vertex buffer, a render pass, a vertex and pixel shader, constants, and a RenderPrimitives call through slots 36-67. None of these has been exercised yet.
part3_what_terrain_and_a_character_requi.shaders_by_name: CreateVertexShader and CreateRenderPass take a std::string name, so shaders are fetched from the resource system by name rather than compiled from bytes here. That ties shader use to the asset system.
part3_what_terrain_and_a_character_requi.textures: CreateTexture takes raw bytes, but the bytes come from game archives.
part3_what_terrain_and_a_character_requi.terrain_data: terrain lives in the game map archives; reaching it requires FileSystem::OpenFile or OpenFullFilePath plus the world/level loading code the game runs when a level is entered.
part3_what_terrain_and_a_character_requi.character_data: the initial character needs a model, a rig, animations and equipment state, all from archives, plus the character spawn path.
part3_what_terrain_and_a_character_requi.scene_pipeline: camera matrices, visibility and batching live in the engine subsystems that Engine::Initialize stands up but that have never been driven.

part4_verdict.verdict: Rendering terrain and a character is not a matter of a few more calls. It requires the asset system (FileSystem plus archive decoding) and the scene/level pipeline, neither of which has been exercised.
realistic_next_steps: prove the geometry path with a single triangle built from our own vertex data (no assets)
then prove FileSystem can open a real game archive and read a known file
then find the level-load entry the game uses when a character enters a map
part4_verdict.do_not_claim: A visible pure colour frame is not a picture of the game world.

boundary: The host published the engine global. Presentation came from the shipped renderer.
